reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 House roll calls, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 22. Nay or No: 4. Not Voting: 14. said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.

posts.text: .@UArkansas alumni are making an impact in our nation’s capital, and I enjoyed meeting with many of them and UofA leadership this week alongside Senator @JohnBoozman and @RepWesterman. Ensuring the University is well resourced is one of my main priorities in Congress, and I am glad to see that work paying off in excellent student outcomes.

While we can never fully repay the debt of gratitude we owe our nation’s veterans for their service, Congress has a responsibility to strengthen the systems and resources that contribute to their well-being. This week, I was proud to support two pieces of legislation that help ensure our veterans receive the support they have earned.

Read more: https://t.co/fOnriSeNMJ

My favorite part about visiting @WestPoint_USMA is seeing the exceptional cadets who hail from Arkansas’s Third District. Today, I had the chance to eat lunch with Cadets Casey Elliot of Springdale, Josiah McCullough of Lowell, Jacob McCrary of Garfield, Chris Monk of Fort Smith, and Carlee Casteel of Rogers.
Ahead of Saturday’s matchup between Army and Air Force, I joined the @BNKonFOX team on a tour of the @WestPoint_USMA campus. Go Army, Beat Air Force! https://t.co/QBduBmbLp2

With @WestPoint_USMA cadets from the Policy Club, @BudgetHawks’ Maya MacGuineas and I had a thoughtful conversation about how our $40 trillion national debt poses serious risks to our ability to respond to future threats. 

As Chairman of the West Point Board of Visitors, I know firsthand the high caliber of our cadets. Challenging these bright, driven young leaders to think critically about our nation’s fiscal future is an investment I hope will pay dividends for years to come.

At @WestPoint_USMA today, I met with Dean of the Academic Board Brig. Gen. Nicholas Gist and other leaders alongside @BudgetHawks’ Maya MacGuineas. Together, we discussed how we can create opportunities for West Point cadets to study the impact of fiscal responsibility on national security.

I will certainly miss Retired Air Force Lt. Gen. Jay Silveria as president of the University of Arkansas System. He has done an outstanding job leading the state’s largest higher education system and building a strong foundation for the future. I wish him all the best in his next chapter and the Board success as it begins the search for his successor.

ICYMI, I joined Senator @JohnBoozman in welcoming Acting @SecArmy Adam Telle to #AR3 last week.

This afternoon, I had the honor of speaking at the dedication of the new Madison Marsh Avenue in Fort Smith.
 
When Madison was a senior at Southside High School, I proudly nominated her to the United States Air Force Academy (USAFA). She graduated from USAFA in 2023 and was crowned Miss America in 2024, making her the first active duty servicemember to win the title.
 
Today, Madison is a First Lieutenant in the United States Air Force and a continued advocate for pancreatic cancer research. I am incredibly proud of her hard work and accomplishments.

I appreciated getting an update on the progress of Phase 2 of the Greenwood Bypass from Mayor Doug Kinslow and his team. In 2024, I was proud to secure $5 million in federal funding to support this project and am currently working on getting an additional $5 million signed into law.

Once completed, the bypass will mean better infrastructure, less congestion downtown, and a more reliable route to work, school, medical care, and more.

At Alpha Packaging, Inc. today, I saw how their team manufactures corrugated boxes and packaging supplies in Greenwood. This family-owned company delivers their products throughout a 300-mile radius and employs over 100 individuals in the River Valley. https://t.co/nWsEkljLDb

It always makes me happy to see students take their learning to the next level. Today, I visited one of the Ignite Professional Studies campuses that serve high school students in the Bentonville School District. Ignite students deep dive into a discipline of their choosing, jumpstarting their professional development and setting them up for future success.

In Van Buren, Fred and Shirley Williams showed me around their multi-generation cattle operation, Fair Oaks Farm, where they raise registered Angus and Angus-Wagyu crosses. During my visit, we also discussed the challenges that producers face and how Congress can support family-owned farms like their own.

This morning, I was in Crawford County with Mountainburg Mayor Susan Wilson, Senator @JohnBoozman,  and USDA Rural Development State Director David Branscum to celebrate the completion of Phase 1 of Mountainburg’s water system improvement project and highlight the role federal investment plays in delivering results.

USDA Rural Development awarded Mountainburg $8.9 million to help fund Phase 1, supporting the installation of miles of new water lines to bring potable water to previously unserved areas of north-central Crawford County.

But there is still work to do, which is why I secured $4.4 million through the appropriations process to help fund Phase 2 and ensure more families have access to clean, safe drinking water on demand.

The opening of the wellness center remains one of my proudest https://t.co/d99OF2WAXM

BIG news: $23 million is headed to Crawford County to help @myARDOT build truck parking infrastructure along I-49! 

This funding is part of the $200 million I allocated to @USDOT in my FY26 Transportation-HUD appropriations bill.

As Chairman of the @HouseAppropsGOP THUD Subcommittee, I know how critical safe and accessible trucking parking is to our nation’s drivers, and I’m extremely proud that #AR3 is directly benefiting from this investment.

The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) plays an important role in strengthening our national security by maintaining critical civilian and military infrastructure across the country. USACE Little Rock District Commander COL Walter Allard and I discussed some of the Corps’ projects in Arkansas’s Third District such as the progress being made on the Foreign Military Sales (FMS) F-35 training center at Ebbing Air National Guard Base, as well as their work on the White River Basin Water Resource Management Study—a study I helped fund through the appropriations process.

Thirty years in the Arkansas Army National Guard taught me that the Guard is not a force of last resort. It is a combat-tested force serving our country at home and abroad.

We cannot continue to ask our Guardsmen to execute today’s missions with yesterday’s equipment. Their responsibilities demand proper funding and modernization as an indispensable force to America’s future.

Read more in my latest op-ed in @WashTimesOpEd:
Farmers are the foundation of America’s economy.  Today on #NationalFarmersDay, we celebrate the men and women who grow and raise the food that fuels our families and nation. https://t.co/iP2PJuV52D

Also there was my good friend, the 59th USMA Superintendent, Lt. Gen. Robert Caslen, Retired. He and I made our way to the field, where we watched the Black Knights warm up for their last second victory against the Green Wave. 

Congratulations to @ArmyWP_Football for an amazing game today! #GoArmy #BeatTulane

Before the Black Knights took on Tulane today, I had the opportunity to watch cadets conduct a “pass and review,” a traditional military parade to display of the Corps of Cadets. After these young men and women exceeded all expectations, the West Point Parachute Team descended from the skies to showcase their skills for all to see.
Go Army, Beat Tulane! https://t.co/ZpJnxHv81y

My visit to @WestPoint_USMA also included a tour of the construction taking place on Goethals Hall—the Academy’s newest building and future Cyber and Engineering Academic Center. Goethals Hall builds on the Academy’s ongoing modernization efforts to prepare students for the challenges of tomorrow, and I am proud to support them in this endeavor through my position on the House Appropriations Defense Subcommittee.

I was joined by @WestPoint_USMA Superintendent Lt. Gen. James Bartholomees, @SenJoniErnst, and @SenTimKaine to have lunch with the West Point cadets today. I always appreciate getting to sit down with these leaders to hear firsthand about their studies and training. It was also great to see Cadet Casey Elliot—Har-Ber High School Class of 2026—in the Mess Hall.

During our meeting, I also presented Dr. @FrankLuntz with a plaque recognizing his service and support to USMA since 2023. West Point will certainly miss Dr. Luntz on campus, but we wish him well on his new chapter. https://t.co/nZsqHNdaD4

Earlier today, I led a meeting with the @WestPoint_USMA Board of Visitors (BOV) in my role as Chairman. United States Military Academy (USMA) leadership briefed us on how the institution is executing on its academic, physical, and military priorities to train and develop the next generation of commissioned Army officers.

One of my favorite parts of visiting @WestPoint_USMA  is getting to check in on the impressive cadets from Arkansas’s Third District. Before this morning’s Board of Visitors’ meeting, I got to see Cadet Ryan Johnson—Bentonville High School Class of 2025—as he gave @RepPatHarrigan  and I a demonstration of flying the Storm King Drone.

Congratulations to #AR3’s @Wolfspeed!

Earlier today, I attended the grand opening for the newly expanded Arkansas Children's Northwest Hospital. This new space will allow the hospital to continue providing top-notch pediatric care to families in the greater Northwest Arkansas region. I'm grateful to the hospital’s leadership and healthcare professionals who work daily to keep our youth healthy.

At Game Aerospace in Bentonville this afternoon, I had the pleasure of introducing two hopeful cadets to leaders of the Department of the Air Force and the United States Air Force Academy. https://t.co/NU2ui0TAjn

Our delegation delivered for all Arkansans by modernizing our nation’s most crucial farm safety net programs in the Working Families Tax Cuts law. I am proud to have helped deliver this much-needed support to the men and women who work tirelessly to provide our nation’s food, fiber, and fuel.

On October 7, 2023, Hamas terrorists massacred more than 1,000 men, women, and children and kidnapped hundreds more—including Americans—in a highly coordinated and ruthless attack. 

Today, we remember the innocent lives that were taken that day, the hostages who endured the unspeakable, and the families of every victim. We must continue to condemn any and all acts of terrorism and antisemitism against Israel.

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
